questions.question: Why does a new Strategy 10-Q stop the weekly refresh from merging instead of being parsed automatically?
options: EDGAR blocks automated 10-Q downloads
10-Qs are filed in PDF only
The refresh runs only on Mondays
Anchor counts come from filing sections the weekly parsers don't read, and a wrong anchor moves every week
questions.explanation: Decision O4: refresh exits 2, the PR stays open and an issue asks a person to reanchor.

questions.question: SharpLink files holdings only on some dates. How did the project add it?
options: Weekly rows with holdings carried forward
Rows only on the dates its filings state ETH holdings
Monthly rows interpolated between filings
Holdings taken from strategicethreserve.xyz
questions.explanation: Decision L1: carried-forward weeks would show numbers no filing states, so SBET has rows on 6/16, 6/28, 6/30 and 8/03 only.

questions.question: You move PREF_ANCHOR_DATE to 2026-09-30 with new Q3 notional values. Which weeks' F can change?
options: Only weeks after 2026-09-30
Only the 2026-09-30 week
Every week, because rolled() backs out flows for weeks before the anchor
None; F is read from the 8-Ks
questions.explanation: rolled() adds flows after the anchor and subtracts flows between a week and the anchor, so every week's level derives from the one anchor. The PR must diff every MSTR row.

questions.question: Today STRC notional rolls to 9,316,191,300 at 2026-09-20. The Q3 10-Q states a different 9/30 figure and no 8-K reports STRC flows between 9/21 and 9/30. What should the reanchor PR do with the gap?
options: State it in the PR as a flow no 8-K reported and trace it to a filing if one exists
Ignore it; the new anchor wins
Add a synthetic retire_pref row to close it
Keep the Q2 anchor
questions.explanation: Every number must trace to a filing and there is no synthetic data (data.md). The gap between the old roll and the new anchor is reported, not filled with an invented action row.

questions.question: You add firm XXXX with parser, balances builder and site entries, but forget dat/engine.py. What happens today?
options: engine raises KeyError on XXXX
XXXX is skipped by engine.main(), and states() would send it to the SBET branch without an error if called
XXXX gets MSTR's converts
pytest fails on test_steps_order
questions.explanation: engine.main() loops over ('BMNR', 'MSTR', 'SBET'), and states() ends in an else for SBET. That is why Project B makes each firm an explicit branch that raises on an unknown one.
